goal: Determine whether a causal posterior that selects its own interventions learns faster than uniform random and deterministic balanced intervention schedules with the same feedback and query budget, while exactly continuing from a cold serialized state.
hypothesis: Active predictive-disagreement interventions improve final held Brier on genuine unknown two-parent worlds by >=0.010 over EACH control (balanced and uniform random), and paired 95% CI lower bound for each improvement >0; no more than +0.010 Brier worsening on unary worlds, +0.020 on three-parent parity/random negative worlds; 100% exact synthetic cold continuation parity.

design.contexts: Two isolated context-labeled worlds A then B per seed; A replayed after B (synthetic cold checkpoint continuation test). No hidden world ID or causal parent identity visible to learner, only public context ID.
design.inputs: five independently chosen binary intervention settings, 32 possible actions; output one binary consequence with 5% independent noise except random case; world source synthetically sampled from 10 genuinely two-parent Boolean truth tables or single-parent copy/invert, three-parent parity, fair random independent label.
design.held_schedule: all 32 possible intervention vectors, each with one deterministic source-noise outcome independent of the learner and disjoint from fit noise; immutable held labels are NEVER used for posterior updates or action decisions
design.cold_continuation: after 12 actions per A/B, serialize full log posterior, per-action visit counts and step counter, independently deserialize twice, resume FOUR A actions on both restored objects with same deterministic action-indexed outcome function, demand bitwise identical action decisions, predictions and serialized state at every continuation step; score held before continuation, no scientific cold process/reboot claim
design.world_and_noise: synthetic xorshift32 world priors; outcome flip determined by a distinct stateless 32-bit seed/world/action/visit counter hash, so all policies receive identical result when choosing the same action and visit count; held outcomes from a disjoint seed domain
design.model: All arms share exactly the same known-class Bayesian mixture with 113 hypotheses (three zero-parent: 0.05/0.5/0.95; ten unary: five input bits x two polarities; 100 two-parent: ten distinct input pairs x ten genuinely two-parent Boolean truth tables), per-order prior mass 1/3, fixed independent 0.05 noise on deterministic hypotheses. No trained external teacher or access to private world labels.

arms.active: At each step compute posterior-predictive Bernoulli probabilities for all 32 candidate actions; choose action maximizing binary entropy of p (equivalently expected mutual information under all deterministic hypotheses with identical 5% noise); break near-equal entropy ties at 1e-12 by smallest prior visits of the action, then smallest x.
arms.balanced: At each step compute SAME full 32-action predictive vector for accounted compute but select deterministic action (11 * step + seed mod 32 + 13 * context) mod 32. Visits unique during first 12; no response-derived adaptivity.
arms.uniform_random: At each step compute SAME predictive vector for accounted compute but select x from an independently seeded xorshift32 stream keyed by seed/context/step; duplicates allowed; no outcome-derived adaptivity.

design.training_update: Bayesian log-likelihood update from observed action consequence only, stable log-sum-exp, no teacher inference. Same model, prior, outcome function, action budget and posteriors for all three arms.
design.cost: Each arm forced to compute 32 posterior action predictions per training step; model evaluation and observations matched. This is an artificial compute-equalized diagnostic; efficient fixed/random controls need only one prediction if implemented normally. Report both forced matched work and minimal baseline practical work; no compute or wall-clock advantage claim.
design.checkpoint: Per context 113 float64 log scores + 32 uint8 action-visit counters + 1 uint8 step => 937 bytes; two contexts =1874 packed bytes; neither JS process overhead nor code/hypothesis dictionary counted; immutable hypothesis dictionary shared by all arms. 4-step continuation after restore must match bitwise.
audit: No teacher access, no native Yggdrasil first-use
All three arms use identical outcome function and held labels per world
Cold A continuation after B identical from two independent deserializations
Uniform random action stream independent of outcomes
Candidate list consists exactly of 113 hypotheses
Out-of-family three-parent parity and random labels retained as negative controls

analysis.primary: Mean per-world post-12 held Brier over 64 pair seeds x2 worlds, compare active to each control with paired by-seed differences and 95% normal CI; active gain = Brier_control - Brier_active.
analysis.secondary: Unary seed family and out-of-family 3-parent parity and random families: mean Brier differences, rejection of any large active-induced worsening. Exact full-domain truths and binary noisy outcomes shared across policies.
analysis.pass_classification: SCIENTIFIC_DEVELOPMENT_SIGNAL_ACTION_CHOICE only if every frozen condition passes; never assert native, transfer, intelligence or self-assembly superiority. Otherwise NO_GO or MIXED depending number of passed gates; retain negatives.
resource_reporting: posterior hypothesis evaluation counts per arm for actual forced-equal scans
per-run host wall time if available
analysis.warning: Known grammar, known 5% sensor noise and public context IDs are structural priors. Posterior predictive action selection uses existing standard active-learning math, not an original general causal intelligence mechanism.
